messages.author: 6fd1fccedadfe847
messages.subject: Nested MANOVA with 3 factors
parts:
Hi,
One of my models for MANOVA includes hierarchy of 3 factors nested model. I read that 2 factors are the current limit of "nested.update" and I will have to divide them.
Should I divide them also in the procD.lm, or only in the nested.update? Is it statistically ok to use the middle factor twice?
Thanks,
Avi

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Nested MANOVA with 3 factors
parts:
Avi,

If you have a model like this, Y ~ A/B/C, you can use nested.update twice to adjust the F values.

For example,

fit <- procD.lm(Y ~ A/B/C, …)
fit <- nested.update(fit, ~B/C)
fit <- nested.update(fit, ~A/B)
summary(fit)

I’m not sure what you mean by using the middle factor twice, but I suppose it is possible to have a model like, Y ~ A/C + B/C.  If that is the case, then the protocol would be,

fit <- procD.lm(Y ~ A/C + B/C, …)
fit <- nested.update(fit, ~B/C)
fit <- nested.update(fit, ~A/C)
summary(fit)

Hope that helps,
Mike

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Nested MANOVA with 3 factors
parts:
Avi,

You might have to make your original fit as

fit <- procD.lm(Y ~ A/B + B/C)

When R encounters a formula as Y ~A/B, it expands it to Y ~ A + A/B.  Writing it as Y ~ A/B is just a short-cut.  I suggested the Y ~A/B/C approach, but I did not consider how it might be expanded, internally.  Apparently it did not include B as fixed effect in reference to C.  

If you have further trouble, you might consider

fit <- procD.lm(Y ~ A + B + A/B + B/C)

And if neither or these do not work, then I’m afraid you have run into a limitation for what the nested.update function can do.  We would like to make this function more universal, ideally, but it’s not an easy one to program for all situations.

Hopefully one of those solutions works.

Mike
